newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen down on high bank rates, loans.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen down on high bank rates, loans.

text.p: Thai stocks were expected to decline on Friday on investor concerns over an increase in banks' lending rates and on worries over the banks' non-peforming loan figures due out soon, brokers said.

"The market sentiment outlook remains weak. Investors are expected to sell on concerns about increases of banks' lending rates and on figures of non-performing loans expected to be released soon," said Payuha Boonsiri of Nithipat Capital.
The composite SET index closed 2.72 points higher at 634.00 on 4.7 billion baht turnover on Thursday. The SET-50 index rose 0.41 point to 47.68.
Four major Thai banks just raised their minimum lending rates by 100 basis points.
They include Bangkok Bank, Thai Farmers, Siam Commercial and Krung Thai.

So far Siam City Bank is the only bank that has announced its non-performing loans. It said they stood at 7.16 percent of total lending at end-June. Other banks are due to release their non-performing loan figures shortly.
